messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - Canary deploy 2026-03-15T02:00Z reporting error-rate spike in eu-west-1 for model-serving-v2 (canary). 5m error-rate 500s = 11% (baseline 0.3%). p95 latency 1.8s -> 6.4s. Affected route: /v1/generate. Incident ID: INC-3098765432

alex: Ack. I'm on it — starting triage. Can someone grab logs + metrics and confirm blast radius?

jordan: digging in. canary weight was at 12% after rollout. Early sign: a subset of pods are returning 502/504s and long tails. I'm seeing repeated KV cache misses then eviction churn in the logs.

maya: looking at pod logs for model-serving-v2-canary. Seeing OOM-ish GC spikes and repeated `kv_cache_miss` followed by `cache_evict` lines. Also some workers showing `session affinity overloaded` logs. Pasting snippet:

```
kv_cache_miss key=prefix:abc123 size=0
cache_evict reclaimed=42MB free=120MB
worker_gc pause=3276ms rss=7.8G
rpc: send error: connection reset by peer
```

alex: @jordan @maya okay. This fits a degraded-canary profile where affinity + cache pressure creates load hotspots. Impact? external customers?

jordan: current numbers: 12% of total traffic routed to canary in eu-west-1. Error-rate among canary users ~11% 500s; global error-rate bump ~0.8% (some fallback logic shows). Top impacted customers appear to be two partner integrations and some internal dogfood clusters.

tim: I can try quick mitigation: reduce canary weight to 0, or flip the feature flag back to previous model. Which do we want first? Reducing weight will stop new traffic to canary but won't drain existing sticky sessions. Flipping flag will route all new requests to stable.

alex: priority = stop user impact quickly. Do both: set canary weight -> 0 and flip feature flag. Jordan, can you do flag flip? Tim, reduce weight and start draining failing pods.

jordan: executing flag rollback now: `redwoodctl flags set model_serving_v2_canary=false --env=eu-west-1`

incident-bot: Action recorded: flag change requested by jordan for model_serving_v2_canary.

jordan: done. API shows `model_serving_v2_canary=false`. Confirmed new sessions are not being routed to canary.

tim: scaling canary weight -> 0 via rollout API: `rolloutctl set-weight canary-2026-03-15 0 --region eu-west-1`

incident-bot: Rollout weight change initiated by tim.

tim: triggered pod drain on all canary instances (graceful), and triggered restart on 3 pods that showed repeated GC stalls. Command used:

```
kubectl -n inference rollout pause deployment/model-serving-v2-canary
kubectl -n inference delete pod model-v2-canary-abc123 model-v2-canary-def456 model-v2-canary-ghi789
```

maya: after drain + restarts, seeing immediate drop in 500s from 11% -> 3.2% in the canary group within two minutes. p95 improved to 2.1s. But some sessions remain sticky; small tail of errors persists.

alex: good. Early customer impact notes: CS notified for two partners (IDs P-112, P-237). @cs-anna can you update them with initial mitigation and ETA?

cs-anna: on it. I'll send a short note: "We've detected elevated errors for requests routed to a canary model in eu-west-1; we've rolled back the canary and are restarting nodes. We're monitoring and will update within 15 minutes." Will ping if they ask for RCA/compensations.

jordan: looking further — root cause candidate: an affinity change in the runtime coupled with an aggressive in-memory KV cache eviction policy introduced in v2. Under realistic request distributions (long-tail user sessions), we see sustained cache misses that force the model runtime to recompute prefixes, which blows up CPU/RSS on a subset of hosts leading to RPC timeouts. There's also a subtle bug where session affinity wasn't honoring new drain headers so clients kept hitting the busy hosts.

alex: notes for post-incident: 1) revert aggressive cache policy, 2) make drain headers respected immediately, 3) improve canary traffic shaping to avoid >5% sticky-bound allocations, 4) more observability around kv miss rates and per-host tail latencies.

tim: temp mitigation I did: increased replica count of stable model-serving pods in eu-west-1 by +2 to absorb traffic while canary drains. Also added a routing guard to prevent redirecting existing sticky sessions back to canary.

incident-bot: Update: error-rate now 1.1% global, canary-specific 0.6%. System health: partial degraded -> recovering.

maya: I've pulled heap/stack traces from the worst hosts and opened a debug run to reproduce cache churn locally. Also collecting a reduced dump for research.

jordan: rollback of canary is still visible in the control plane; full traffic shifts should complete in ~8-12 minutes (sticky sessions expire). Will monitor for re-entrance.

alex: any signs of customer facing data loss or incorrect outputs?

maya: no incorrect outputs observed. Failures are mostly 502/504 or timeouts. No PII exposure, no data corruption.

tim: one more quick check: ingress logs show that a small fraction (~0.4%) of requests were retried and served from fallback stable model which increased latency for those users. We'll note that in impact.

alex: status update to channel in 10. If stable after 15m, we will close initial pager. If issues persist, we'll escalate to infra lead @jordan and oncall-2.

(8m later)

incident-bot: [UPDATE] 3098765432 - canary rollback in progress. Global 5m error-rate 500s = 0.9%. p95 latency 1.5s.

jordan: verified control plane shows 0% weight for canary and all production traffic on stable. No new canary allocations. I'm recommending we keep canary paused until we have a patch.

alex: agreed. Jordan, please open a follow-up ticket and assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml for kernel/cache fixes. Maya, include reproducer + logs. Tim, revert replica increases when you confirm stable baseline.

jordan: ticket created: INF-11702 - "canary: kv-cache eviction + affinity overload causing tail latency". Assigned: eng-runtime (primary), eng-ml (secondary). Included debug data and initial mitigation steps.

maya: note: we should add a synthetic test simulating sticky-session heavy traffic with colder cache to our canary harness. I'll draft test cases.

tim: scaling back stable replicas to baseline now.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE] 3098765432 - Incident moved to monitoring. Severity: P2 (recovered but requires follow-up).

alex: handing off to night oncall @maria for continued monitoring and RCA follow-up. Handoff notes:
- Issue: canary model-serving-v2 induced kv-cache churn + affinity bug -> ephemeral 5xx and latency spike.
- Mitigations: feature flag flipped -> false, canary weight -> 0, canary pods drained/restarted, stable replicas temporarily increased then scaled back.
- Impact: ~12% of EU-west canary users saw elevated 5xx (peak 11%) during window. Global bump ~0.9% total error-rate. No data loss. Customers P-112 and P-237 notified.
- Action items: INF-11702 (patch cache policy + affinity respect), add synthetic canary test, consider limiting sticky assignment during canary to 2% until harness validated, add alert for kv_cache_miss rate per host.
- Contacts: eng-runtime (jordan), infra (tim), eng-ml (maya), CS (cs-anna).

maria: taking handoff. I'll keep watch for 2 hours, will post again on status. Thanks all.

cs-anna: thanks, team. I'll follow up with customers after final confirm of full recovery.

alex: thanks everyone for the quick run. Closing active pager, moving to postmortem phase. :white_check_mark:
